name: Reclaim.ai
summary: Auto-schedules tasks, habits and meetings around your stated priorities. Google Calendar-first, so Outlook-heavy teams are out, and the free tier is limited.
best_for: Google Calendar teams that want AI to auto-schedule tasks, habits and meetings around their priorities
skip_if: you run hosted or on-premise Exchange, which Reclaim's help centre lists as unsupported, or you don't overbook your calendar — the auto-scheduling has little to optimize
honest_knock: The magic only works on a calendar it can write to. Google Calendar was first, but Microsoft 365, Outlook.com and Exchange-backed accounts are supported too (reclaim.ai/integrations/outlook-calendar, read 15 September 2026); Reclaim's own help centre still lists hosted and on-premise Exchange as unsupported. The free tier is quite limited. A genuine time-saver for the right setup, useless for the wrong one.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-03 on their own pricing page, USD) Four levels, and the page keeps both billing terms in the markup rather than recomputing them. Lite is free forever for a single user. Billed yearly the seats are Starter $10, Business $15 and Enterprise $22 per seat a month; billed monthly Starter is $12 and Business $18, and the monthly column prints no Enterprise figure at all. Enterprise carrying a list price is new here — we described it as quote-only until this reading, and Business had no number in our dossier at all. Seats are capped by tier rather than open: 1 user on Lite, up to 10 on Starter, up to 100 on Business and over 100 on Enterprise, with the AI-agent allowance per seat stepping 5, 10, 100 and unlimited beside them. The mechanism most reviews miss is Attendee Units, and it survives this redesign even though the plan cards no longer mention it. AUs are attendees without a paid Reclaim seat in Smart Meetings of 3 or more people (two-person meetings do not need them), and they accumulate across a team account. Extra AUs are bought in packs on top of the seat, and the packs follow the same two terms. On yearly billing Starter packs run $8 for 3, $16 for 6, $24 for 9 and $32 for 12, and Business $12 for 6, $24 for 12, $36 for 18 and $48 for 24; billed monthly those become $10/$20/$30/$40 and $15/$30/$45/$60. Enterprise packs are $18 for 10, $36 for 20, $54 for 30 and $72 for 40 on either term. Each extra pack also includes a free seat of the same tier to assign to a team member: a Starter seat with every 3-pack, a Business seat with every 6-pack and an Enterprise seat with every 10-pack. If you schedule across people who do not have seats, the AU packs rather than the seat price are what determines your bill. One caveat on that arithmetic: the page still carries a launch-promo line saying AUs are 100% free through July 31st, a date that has passed, so confirm at checkout whether the packs are billing yet. Discount codes appear periodically; on 14 September a banner offered 30% off Starter and Business to new users, and on 3 October 2026 it read "20% off with code MEETINGS".
